did_you_know.text: Did you know? The prophecy in this chapter is directed against the Philistines, and it was given before Pharaoh struck Gaza.
Did you know? The approaching army is described as waters rising from the north and becoming a rushing stream, capable of flooding the land, its cities, and its inhabitants.
Did you know? The sound of the horses’ hooves, the chariots, and the wheels is described as causing such great terror that fathers do not turn to their sons because their hands are limp with fear.
Did you know? The prophecy describes the day when all the Philistines will be plundered, and it also mentions Tyre and Sidon and the loss of every remnant that could help them.
Did you know? The Philistines are also called “the remnant of the island of Caphtor,” an expression referring to their origin or connection with Caphtor.
Did you know? Gaza and Ashkelon are mentioned by name among the cities that will be affected: Gaza will become bald, and Ashkelon is described as silenced and desolate.
Did you know? The sword is personified: it is asked how long it will be before it becomes quiet, and it is told to return to its sheath.
Did you know? The sword cannot be quiet because the Lord has commanded it to act against Ashkelon and the seashore.
